get.summary: The process can reach the database.

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code to an email address or phone number. Answers the
same way whether or not an account exists for it. Codes sent earlier keep
working until they expire, up to the newest few.

422.description: Not an email address or phone number

429.description: Too many codes requested for this identifier or from this address (`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`), or too many wrong codes for this identifier today, so none is sent (`TOO_MANY_GUESSES`)

delete.summary: Signs out: the session stops working everywhere it was held.

post.summary: Signs in with a one-time code, creating the account on first use.

401.description: The code is wrong, expired or used up

429.description: Too many wrong codes for this identifier today (`TOO_MANY_GUESSES`), or a wrong code from an address that has offered too many this hour (`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`)

get.summary: The people the caller has blocked, most recently blocked first.

200.description: Each by an exchange shared with them

get.summary: The caller's exchanges, most recently changed first.

200.description: Exchanges the caller is a party to

post.summary: Starts an exchange as a private draft.

get.summary: One exchange, as its party sees it.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

get.summary: Whether the caller has blocked the other party of this exchange.

200.description: The caller's own block, if any

404.description: No such exchange for this account

put.summary:
Blocks the other party of this exchange. Neither of the two can then join
an exchange the other starts. Whatever is waiting to be signed between
them is withdrawn or declined; an agreement in force stays in force. The
other party is not told.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Nobody has joined the exchange yet

delete.summary: Removes the caller's block on the other party of this exchange.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Nobody has joined the exchange yet

post.summary:
Does one thing to an exchange: accept, decline or withdraw a revision,
act on a contribution, confirm or reject whoever claimed the invitation,
discard a draft, or end or close it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per attempt to make this change

200.description: Done; the exchange as it now stands

403.description: That is for the other party to do

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Refused by the rules, or the exchange changed

put.summary: Saves the caller's unsent working copy.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

get.summary:
What has happened in an exchange, oldest first, with what the parties
wrote along the way: the message sent with a revision, a note on a claim,
the reason for a dispute, a statement. Answers with the latest events, 50
unless `limit` says otherwise and never more than 200; `earlier` in the
answer is the `before` that reads the page before.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return events before this sequence number. Leave out for the latest.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many events to return: 50 unless said, 200 at most.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

post.summary: Replaces the invitation link. The previous link stops working.

200.description: The new link token, shown once

409.description: Someone is in the invited party's place

post.summary:
Gives up the invited party's place. For someone who opened an invitation
link and has not been confirmed by the initiator: it is their way out,
since they cannot decline. Anything they signed is void, and from then on
the exchange does not exist for them.

403.description: The initiator cannot leave their own exchange

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: The caller has been confirmed, and is a party for good

get.summary:
The record of an exchange as one self-contained document, for a party to
keep or hand to someone else: how it stands, every revision sent with
what it says and what became of it, every signature and what it rests
on, and everything that happened, in order.
get.description:
One document holds at most 500 events, and at most 50 revisions or about
a megabyte of their text, whichever comes first. A longer record
continues in further documents: `part.next` holds the two values to ask
for the next one with, and `part.complete` says when one document is all
of it.

parameters.name: revisions_after
parameters.description:
Continue after the revision with this sequence number. Taken from
`part.next` of the part before.

parameters.name: events_after
parameters.description:
Continue after the event with this sequence number. Taken from
`part.next` of the part before.

200.description: The record, or one part of it

404.description: No such exchange for this account

post.summary:
Reports an exchange, and with it the other party, for review. The other
party is not told. Reporting the same exchange again while the first
report is open changes nothing and is answered the same way.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Nobody has joined the exchange yet

422.description: Details too long, or missing for `OTHER`

post.summary:
Sends a revision, which signs it: a first proposal, a counteroffer, or an
amendment to an agreement in force. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so a
retry cannot send it twice.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per attempt to make this change

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Refused by the rules, or the exchange changed

post.summary: Takes the invited party's place in the exchange.

200.description: Claimed; the exchange as the new party sees it

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

post.summary:
Shows the proposal behind an invitation link. No sign-in needed. The token
travels in the body so it never appears in a URL the service logs.

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

post.summary:
Reports the proposal behind an invitation link, and with it the person
who sent it. No sign-in needed: the token is the proof of having received
it, as for the preview, and travels in the body for the same reason. A
link that shows no preview takes no report.

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

409.description: The link is the caller's own

422.description: Details too long, or missing for `OTHER`

patch.summary: Changes the display name or language, or records that the holder is an adult.

get.summary: What deleting the account would do to the exchanges it is in. Changes nothing.

post.summary:
Deletes the signed-in account. Every session ends, its email address and
phone number are released, its working data is removed, and each exchange
it is still in is ended or put on the way to closing. Agreements the
other party signed stay in that party's record. It cannot be undone.

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong, expired, used up or was sent for something else

422.description: The account has no such identifier

429.description: Too many wrong deletion codes from this account today

503.description: The account was busy and nothing was done; the code still works

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code for deleting the account to its own email address
or phone number. The code is good for that and nothing else. Requests are
counted against the account, apart from sign-in codes, so nobody asking
for sign-in codes for the same address can use them up.

422.description: The account has no such identifier

429.description: Too many deletion codes requested by this account

post.summary:
Verifies a second identifier and attaches it to the account, or replaces
the one of the same kind. An account with both a verified email and a
verified phone can meet the higher risk tier.

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong

409.description: The identifier belongs to another account

422.description: Not an email address or phone number

429.description: Too many wrong codes for this identifier today (`TOO_MANY_GUESSES`), or a wrong code from an address that has offered too many this hour (`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`)

get.summary: Identifies the service and its build, and says how old a client may be.

adult_confirmed.description: The holder has confirmed they are 18 or over. Required before signing.

display_name.description: Empty until the person has chosen one.

language.description: A supported language tag, such as `en` or `es`.

Actor.description:
Who did something: one of the two parties, or the service acting on a
timer.

code.description: The one-time code sent to it.

identifier.description: An email address, or a phone number in international form.

BlockStatus.description:
Whether the caller has blocked the other party of an exchange. Says
nothing about whether the other party has blocked the caller.

name.description:
The other party's name as the exchange writes it. An exchange closed
before anything was agreed shows no terms to read it from.

BlockedPerson.description:
Someone the caller has blocked, named as an exchange the two share names
them. The exchange is also how to unblock them.

left.description:
Set when the caller is no longer in that exchange and cannot open it:
they had opened its invitation and left before being confirmed. It
still names the person, and unblocking through it still works.

name.description: Their name as written in that exchange.

Claimant.description: Who claimed the invitation, shown to the initiator so they can confirm.

CodeChannel.description: Which of the account's identifiers a code is sent to.

oneOf.description: Sign the open revision.
Take back a revision you sent, before it takes effect.

Throw away a draft that was never sent. It closes with nothing agreed
and leaves the list. Only the initiator has one, and only until the
first revision is sent.

Claim, confirm, dispute or waive a contribution. A dispute needs a
reason, and a claim after a dispute needs a note.
The initiator confirms who claimed the invitation.

The initiator says whoever claimed the invitation is not who they
invited. That person is removed, anything they signed is void, and a
new invitation link can be issued.

Consent.description:
Which consent wording the signer was shown. Signing is refused unless it
is the current version.

language.description: The language the wording was shown in, as a supported language tag.

ConsentShown.description: Which consent wording the signer was shown before signing.

Continuation.description: Where to continue reading a record too long for one document.

amount_minor.description: Whole minor units of the exchange's currency. Money only.

id.description:
Chosen by the client for a new contribution; kept unchanged for one
carried over from an earlier revision.

ContributionRef.description:
A contribution, with its description as the parties wrote it in the
revision the event happened under.

since.description:
When it came to stand this way, RFC 3339. Not sent where it is not
known, such as on an agreement coming into force in the history.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, such as `America/Chicago`. Due dates are read in it.

code.description: The one-time code sent to the identifier.

language.description:
The language the client is showing, as a tag such as `es-MX`. Used only
when this creates the account; an unsupported one becomes the default.

code.description: The one-time code sent for deleting the account.

DeletionPreview.description:
What deleting the account would do to the exchanges it is in, counted, so
that the person can be told before they confirm.

agreements_in_force.description: Agreements in force. Each gets a request to close, in the account's name.

drafts.description: Drafts never sent. They are discarded.

open_proposals.description: Negotiations with an offer on the table. They end with nothing agreed.

Delivery.description: How the client wants to hold the session.

oneOf.description: A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the exchange's timezone.
When the agreement is accepted.
When another contribution in the same revision is accepted.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable codes for every refusal the API can return. Clients map these to
wording in the user's language and never parse message text
(DESIGN.md §13.3). Adding a code here is a contract change: the generated
client makes the shared wording tables fail to compile until it is covered.

EventType.description:
Everything that can happen to an exchange. Events of any other kind are
not part of what the parties are shown.

close_request_lapses_at.description:
When the close request's response window runs out and the exchange
closes unresolved, unless the request is taken back or what is
outstanding is resolved first (DESIGN.md §5.3). RFC 3339. Computed
here, so every client shows the same moment.

contributions.description: Status of each contribution in the agreement in force.

display_code.description: For telling exchanges apart. Not a credential.

draft.description: The viewer's own unsent working copy.

oneOf.description: The agreement currently binding, if any.

invitation_open.description:
Only for the initiator, and only while nobody is in the invited
party's place: whether an invitation link is out that can still be
used. It is not once the link has been used, even by someone since
removed, or has expired; a new one has to be issued.

oneOf.description: The revision awaiting acceptance, if any.

other_party_left.description:
The other party has deleted their account and can no longer act in
this exchange. Said only while the exchange is still open, which is
when the viewer needs to know it. Always sent; a client may read its
absence as `false`.

version.description: Send this back as `expected_version` with the next change.

HistoryPage.description: A stretch of an exchange's history, oldest first.

earlier.description:
Set when there is history before this page: pass it as `before` to
read the page before.

bound_to.description:
Names who the invitation is for: only an account that has verified
this email address or phone number can claim it.

InvitationPreview.description: What someone holding an invitation link sees before signing in.

bound.description: The invitation names a specific person.

currency.description: The exchange's currency, which its amounts are in.

timezone.description: The exchange's IANA timezone, which its due dates are read in.

minimum_client_versions.description:
The oldest build of each client that may still change anything. A
client below its minimum shows that it must be updated; its changes
are refused with `CLIENT_TOO_OLD`. Absent for a client with no minimum.

MinimumClientVersions.description:
The oldest version of each client that may still change anything.
`None` means every version may.

NewInvitationReport.description:
A report on the proposal behind an invitation link, from someone who need
not be signed in. The token is their proof of having received it.

details.description: As for a report on an exchange.

What the reporter wants a reviewer to know. Optional, except with the
reason `OTHER`. At most 2,000 characters.

Notices.description: What a reader of the document needs to be told, in its language.

content_hash.description: How to recompute a content hash.

signatures.description: What a signature here rests on.

statements.description: That what the parties recorded about delivery is theirs alone.

Part.description: Which stretch of the record a document holds.

complete.description: This one document holds the whole record.

from.description: Where this document starts. Zero and zero for the first.

oneOf.description: Where the next one starts, when the record goes on.

Parties.description:
Each party's name as the agreement writes it: the agreement in force, or
the first proposal until there is one.

amount.description: A positive decimal number such as `2` or `1.5`.

RecordContribution.description: Where a contribution of the agreement stands.

since.description: When it came to stand this way. RFC 3339, UTC.

RecordDocument.description:
The record of one exchange, as one self-contained document: a party's
copy to keep or to hand to someone else.

contributions.description:
Where each contribution of the agreement stands. These are the
parties' own statements about delivery; the service did not check
them.

language.description:
The language `notices` and the descriptions are written in. What the
parties wrote is never translated.

prepared_for.description:
Which party this copy was made for. Both parties' copies hold the
same record.

RecordEvent.description:
One entry in the history. The history is append-only: nothing in it is
ever edited or removed, and a correction is a later entry.

by_removed_claimant.description:
Set when the actor was someone who had opened the invitation and was
removed, or left, before the initiator confirmed them. `actor` is
then `B` for the place they were in; they are not the party this
record names as B, and the record does not say who they were.

invitation_named_them.description:
When the invited party joined: whether the invitation named them, so
that no confirmation by the initiator was needed.

note.description:
What the actor wrote with it, exactly as written: the message sent
with a revision, a note on a claim, the reason for a dispute, or a
statement.

oneOf.description: When the exchange closed: how.

The revision the event is about; for an event about a contribution,
the agreement that was in force.

sequence.description: Position in the exchange's history, counting from 1.

signature_void.description:
When whoever opened the invitation was removed or left: whether they
had signed the revision then open, named in `revision`. If so, that
signature is void: it never took effect and never can.

oneOf.description: Where the contribution stood as a result.

statuses.description:
When a revision came into force: where each of its contributions
stood as a result. A contribution of the agreement before that is not
listed was removed by the amendment.

waived.description: When the exchange ended by agreement: what was released, undelivered.

display_code.description: For telling exchanges apart. Not a credential.

oneOf.description: The agreement: in force now, or in force when the exchange closed.

last_event.description: The sequence number of the latest event when this was written.

oneOf.description: The revision waiting to be signed.

timezone.description: The timezone due dates are read in.

RecordRevision.description:
A revision that was sent: what it says, who sent and signed it, and what
became of it.

oneOf.description:
The revision this one answered: the offer it replaced, or the
agreement it proposed to amend.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of `signed` as canonical JSON (RFC 8785), in hex.

expires_at.description: When it would lapse if not signed by both. RFC 3339, UTC.

note.description: The message sent with it. Not part of what is signed.

sequence.description: 1 for the first proposal, counting up.

signatures.description:
The author's, made by sending it, then the other party's if they
accepted. Only signatures that count are here.

signed.description: What the signatures cover, word for word.

void_signatures.description:
Signatures that do not count and never will, kept apart so that
nobody reading `signatures` takes one for the other party's.

ReportReason.description:
Why an exchange is being reported. A fixed list, so that a reviewer can
tell what kind of harm a report is about before reading it.

identifier.description: An email address, or a phone number in international form.

channel.description: Which of the account's own identifiers to send the code to.

RevisionRef.description: A revision, named both ways: by ID, and by the number people see.

sequence.description: 1 for the first proposal, counting up.

invitation_token.description:
The link token for the invited party, returned once, when the first
revision is sent. Only its hash is kept.

in_force_at.description: When it came into force, if it ever did.

oneOf.description: The revision that took its place, where one did.

since.description: When it came to stand this way. RFC 3339, UTC.

RevisionTerms.description: What a revision says: the part both parties sign.

accepted_by.description:
Who has signed it. The author always has. A signature left by someone
who was removed from the invited party's place is not counted.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the signed terms, in hex.

expected_version.description: The exchange version the client last saw.

body.description: The client's working copy, stored as given.

expected_version.description: The exchange version the client last saw.

oneOf.description: Used when this is the first revision, which also issues the invitation.

note.description: A message to the other party. Not part of what is signed.

Signature.description: One party's signature on one exact revision.

content_hash.description: The hash that was signed, in hex. It is the revision's own.

name.description: The signer's name as that revision writes it.

SignedContribution.description: A contribution as it is signed.

amount_minor.description: Whole minor units of the exchange's currency. Money only.

from.description: The party who owes it; the other receives it.

id.description: The same contribution keeps its ID from one revision to the next.

oneOf.description: Money only.

SignedDocument.description:
Exactly what a signature covers. A revision's content hash is the SHA-256
of this object written as canonical JSON (RFC 8785).

attachments.description: SHA-256 of each attached file, in hex.

timezone.description: The timezone due dates are read in.

Slot.description: One side of the exchange. `A` is the initiator, `B` the invited counterparty.

Status.description:
Where a contribution stands. Overdue is derived from `Pending` plus the due
condition; it is not a status.

adult_confirmed.description: Only `true` is meaningful: a confirmation cannot be taken back.

language.description:
A language tag. A regional tag falls back to its base language; an
unsupported language is refused.

Verification.description:
The evidence behind a signature: how the signer had shown the service who
they are. It is all the evidence there is.

description.description: The same, in words, in the document's language.

verified_at.description:
When the signer entered that code, which is when they signed in and
can be earlier than the signature. RFC 3339, UTC.

VoidSignature.description:
A signature that never took effect and never can. It was made by someone
who had opened the invitation and was removed, or left, before the
initiator confirmed them. It is kept because it happened. It names
nobody: that person is not the party the revision names.

content_hash.description: The hash that was signed, in hex.

party.description: The place the signer was in.

void_since.description: When the signer was removed or left. RFC 3339, UTC.
